correctness.rationale: Exact conservative energy establishes the positive-energy ovals. Changing to inverse potential coordinates yields a strictly positive derivative of each fixed-energy force at positive cubic coefficient, proving strict monotonicity for all energies. Beta integral scaling evaluates the two endpoints. Differentiating the root-rescaled nonsingular quadrature at zero cubic parameter gives derivative \(-\sqrt2/(3d)\), with controlled quadratic remainder, hence the high-energy correction and the sharp fourth-power contrast limit. A separate standard-library quadrature checker reproduced a crossover example and asymptotic diagnostics; the proof does not rely on a finite experiment.

originality.rationale: The identified Chen–Li–Yu first version (2023-08-29, Theorem 1.2, case G1) classifies global nilpotent centers and explicitly constructs one-sided Hamiltonians but gives no physical-time occupation comparison in the inspected Hamiltonian and classification arguments. The inspected Yang–Liu–Lu (2024) open full text addresses local period constants for a different switching quartic system. The claimed global strict monotonicity of a side-occupation fraction, the iff single-exchange condition, and the sharp fourth-power contrast divergence are not consequences of the classification or the distinct local-period results without the new inverse-potential argument. Targeted published mathematical-record searches showed no covering statement; absolute priority remains an open risk.

value.rationale: The natural phase-timing observable of a switching global center is how physical time partitions between its two force laws. The source global-center classification establishes orbit closure but cannot decide which side dominates or whether dominance changes with energy. The theorem completely classifies that crossing for all positive coefficients in a motivated subfamily, proves strict monotonicity, and supplies a sharp fourth-power scale for the transition near equal quartic stiffness. These parameter-global dynamical properties are not arbitrary coefficient tests or routine restatements of a period quadrature.
